evidence.reference_title: Axin1 regulates tooth root development by inhibiting AKT1-mTORC1 activation and Shh translation in Hertwig's epithelial root sheath
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that Axin1, a scaffold protein that negatively regulates canonical Wnt signaling, is strongly expressed in the HERS.

evidence.reference_title: Axin1 regulates tooth root development by inhibiting AKT1-mTORC1 activation and Shh translation in Hertwig's epithelial root sheath
evidence.snippet: Axin1 ablation in the HERS of mice leads to defective root development, but in a manner independent of canonical Wnt signaling.

nodes.description: Taurodontism is characterized by an enlarged pulp cavity/chamber.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence of taurodontism: meta-analysis in recent humans and evolutionary perspectives.
evidence.snippet: Taurodontism is a continuous anatomical variation of permanent and primary posterior teeth represented by an enlargement of the pulp cavity.

nodes.description: Root furcation is displaced apically with altered root-trunk configuration.

evidence.reference_title: Epithelial Wnt10a Is Essential for Tooth Root Furcation Morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Wnt10a knockout in the whole tissue (EIIa-Cre;Wnt10aflox/flox) and in dental epithelium (K14-Cre;Wnt10aflox/flox) led to an absence of or apically located root furcation in molars of mice, a phenotype that resembled taurodontism.

nodes.description: In mouse Hertwig epithelial root sheath, Axin1 binds AKT1 and restrains AKT1-mTORC1 signaling and Shh translation; Axin1 ablation produces defective root development independently of canonical Wnt signaling. No human AXIN1 association with taurodontism is recorded, so this node is an experimental root-development mechanism rather than a cause of this entry.

evidence.reference_title: Axin1 regulates tooth root development by inhibiting AKT1-mTORC1 activation and Shh translation in Hertwig's epithelial root sheath
evidence.snippet: Further studies reveal that Axin1 in the HERS negatively regulates the AKT1-mTORC1 pathway through binding to AKT1, leading to inhibition of ribosomal biogenesis and mRNA translation.

evidence.reference_title: Axin1 regulates tooth root development by inhibiting AKT1-mTORC1 activation and Shh translation in Hertwig's epithelial root sheath
evidence.snippet: Sonic hedgehog (Shh) protein, a morphogen essential for root development, is over-synthesized by upregulated mTORC1 activity upon Axin1 inactivation.

nodes.description: Loss of epithelial WNT10A signaling disrupts furcation formation and adjacent mesenchymal cell proliferation (via Wnt4 regulation), driving apically displaced root furcation and taurodont root morphology.

evidence.reference_title: Epithelial Wnt10a Is Essential for Tooth Root Furcation Morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: our study provides the first in vivo evidence that epithelial Wnt10a guides root furcation formation and plays a crucial role in controlling the organized proliferation of adjacent mesenchymal cells by regulating proper Wnt4 expression during root furcation morphogenesis.

nodes.description: Taurodont morphology results from failure or delay of Hertwig epithelial root sheath (HERS) diaphragm horizontal invagination, shifting root furcation apically and expanding the pulp chamber in multirooted teeth.
nodes.id: Failed invagination of Hertwig epithelial root sheath diaphragm

evidence.reference_title: Taurodontism: a review of the condition and endodontic treatment challenges.
evidence.snippet: Taurodontism can be defined as a change in tooth shape caused by the failure of Hertwig's epithelial sheath diaphragm to invaginate at the proper horizontal level.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Variants in KCTD1 Are Associated with Isolated Dental Anomalies
evidence.snippet: Whole exome sequencing identified two unrelated families with rare (p.Arg241Gln) or novel (p.Pro243Ser) variants in KCTD1.

nodes.description: Pathogenic KCTD1 C-terminal variants segregate with isolated taurodontism and related root anomalies, disrupting protein-protein interactions and canonical WNT-SHH-BMP signaling control during human dental morphogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Variants in KCTD1 Are Associated with Isolated Dental Anomalies
evidence.snippet: The variants segregated with the dental anomalies in all nine patients from the two families.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Variants in KCTD1 Are Associated with Isolated Dental Anomalies
evidence.snippet: Functional studies on the p.Arg241Gln variant are consistent with an impact on β-catenin levels and canonical WNT signaling.

nodes.description: Additional teeth can co-occur in genetically associated dental anomaly spectra that include taurodontism.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Variants in KCTD1 Are Associated with Isolated Dental Anomalies
evidence.snippet: Clinical findings of the patients included taurodontism, unseparated roots, long roots, tooth agenesis, a supernumerary tooth, torus palatinus, and torus mandibularis.

nodes.description: Defining radiographic phenotype with enlarged pulp chambers and apical displacement of pulpal floor/furcation in multirooted teeth.

evidence.reference_title: Taurodontism: a review of the condition and endodontic treatment challenges.
evidence.snippet: An enlarged pulp chamber, apical displacement of the pulpal floor, and no constriction at the level of the cementoenamel junction are the characteristic features.

nodes.description: Reduced tooth number is an associated phenotype in KCTD1-associated dental anomaly presentations including taurodontism.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Variants in KCTD1 Are Associated with Isolated Dental Anomalies
evidence.snippet: Clinical findings of the patients included taurodontism, unseparated roots, long roots, tooth agenesis, a supernumerary tooth, torus palatinus, and torus mandibularis.

evidence.reference_title: Taurodontism, variations in tooth number, and misshapened crowns in Wnt10a null mice and human kindreds.
evidence.snippet: WNT10A heterozygotes exhibited molar root taurodontism and mild tooth agenesis (with incomplete penetrance) in their permanent dentitions.

nodes.description: Human WNT10A variants impair canonical Wnt ligand signaling in the dental epithelium and odontoblast lineage, causing molar crown and root furcation dysmorphology; the severity of accompanying tooth agenesis correlates with the number of defective WNT10A alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Taurodontism, variations in tooth number, and misshapened crowns in Wnt10a null mice and human kindreds.
evidence.snippet: WNT10A heterozygotes exhibited molar root taurodontism and mild tooth agenesis (with incomplete penetrance) in their permanent dentitions.

evidence.reference_title: Taurodontism, variations in tooth number, and misshapened crowns in Wnt10a null mice and human kindreds.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that molar crown and root dysmorphologies are caused by WNT10A defects and that the severity of the tooth agenesis correlates with the number of defective WNT10A alleles.
